claude.take: The highest-quality balance sheet of the six and the weakest growth. Manipal prints roughly a third of India's credit and debit cards, throws off 33.6% EBITDA margins and 32.7% RoCE, and has taken borrowings from ₹473 Cr to under ₹1 Cr — this is a real franchise with genuine moat in a regulated, certification-heavy business. But revenue has compounded at 3.4% over three years and FY26 profit actually fell 10%, so at 29.4x FY26 earnings the buyer is paying an 18% premium to its only listed peer for a business going sideways, into a structural headwind of card digitisation. The redeeming feature versus the rest of the week: three-quarters of the fresh issue is actual equipment capex, not debt repayment. The 10% retail quota is the practical catch — small allotments, and a crowded book if QIBs like it.
